text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging eng-oncall — p99 latency breach detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1. Current p99=820ms (SLO=500ms), p95=210ms. Affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream. Auto-escalation to oncall.

maria: saw the page, taking it. Acknowledging. Starting triage.

maria: quick: is this concentrated to a model or across versions? (cc @alex @jamal)

alex: early signal looks correlated with KV cache pressure on runtime nodes serving eu-west-1. Grafana: kv_cache_utilization ~98%, evictions spiking, fragmentation high.

alex: pasted the metric snapshot:
```
metric: runtime.kv_cache.utilization 98.1% (cluster eu-west-1)
metric: runtime.kv_cache.evictions_per_min 3120
metric: runtime.kv_cache.fragmentation 72%
metric: request.latency.p99 820ms
routes: /v1/generate-stream (p99 890ms)
```

maria: nice. Any recent rollout or config change that would increase prefill behavior?

jamal: we rolled a prefill optimization last night to prefetch context early for long chats (PR #4528) — it increased prefill concurrency from 6 -> 16 in the runtime config for streaming workers. I reverted that on staging last hour because of memory spikes, but prod still on 16.

elin: that explains the imbalance: prefill threads filling KV with large prefix entries while decode threads also concurrently increase KV usage, causing eviction churn and tail stalls when a decode misses and has to reconstruct KV from slower store.

maria: hypothesis: prefill vs decode concurrency imbalance -> frequent eviction of hot KV entries -> decode stalls (tail latency). Also fragmentation means we can't allot contiguous cache for big KV chunks so we thrash.

sre-lead: confirm mitigation plan please: short term (minutes), medium (hours), long term (days).

alex: short term: 1) Reduce prefill concurrency on prod streaming workers from 16 -> 4 via runtime feature flag. 2) Temporarily increase KV cache capacity by 20% on eu-west-1 runtime pool. 3) Route heavy streaming traffic to fallback model variant with smaller key footprint (model-small-stream) for 60 minutes.

maria: executing short term steps now. Rolling flag change to prefill.concurrency=4 to runtime group eu-west-1. Patch command:
```
POST /api/infra/runtime/flags/rollout
{ "group": "eu-west-1-streaming", "flag": "prefill.concurrency", "value": 4 }
```

maria: also increasing cache_capacity via infra API to 1.2x for pool eu-west-1-gpu-streaming.

storage-bot: cache resize job queued -> job-id=cis-8842, estimated time 90s.

jamal: I'm going to start traffic shift to model-small-stream for the heaviest routes. Will do canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 10m if stable.

maria: watch metrics during rollout. I'll tail decode logs for stalls.

alex: logs showing decode stall stack traces (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-14T21:05:10Z] decode_worker[13] WARN kv_cache: miss for key=kv_abc123 len=274k -> fallback fetch -> 320ms
[2026-03-14T21:05:11Z] decode_worker[11] ERROR stall detected: waiting on kv rebuild 1.8s
```

maria: started the flag rollout. patch reported success on 12/12 nodes in pool. Observing immediate drop in prefill write QPS.

maria: cache resize completed. storage-bot reports new capacity 1.2x, fragmentation still high but utilization dropped to ~~91%.

jamal: traffic shift at 5% canary started.

elin: monitoring p99 across routes. p99 dropped from 820ms -> 540ms within 4 minutes of the prefill flag change.

sre-lead: good immediate signal. Keep canary and watch for regressions. Document customer impact.

maria: customer impact: partial for EU customers using streaming - some sessions experienced stalls of 2-6s. Estimated affected sessions ~0.3% of total streaming sessions in the hour window. No complete outages; requests still finish eventually. Notifying support to prepare CS messages.

jamal: advancing canary to 25% now. No errors in canary logs so far.

alex: eviction rate trending down: evictions_per_min 3100 -> 900 after both mitigations. kv_cache_utilization -> 86%.

maria: p99 now 430ms for most routes; /v1/generate-stream still has tail at 520ms but trending down.

sre-lead: medium-term (next 12h): 1) Keep prefill.concurrency conservative (4). 2) Add a TTL cap for prefill entries so they don't persist indefinitely. 3) Schedule a slow rolling defragmentation job for KV cache nodes.

elin: long-term (postmortem): revisit prefill strategy — prefer on-demand prefill and eviction-awareness in the prefill scheduler; add admission control so prefill won't evict currently decoding keys. Also consider compacting KV layout (defrag) and stronger allocation algorithms.

maria: handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Jamal will take over oncall for the incident. Jamal, everything you need is in this thread: actions taken, job ids, dashboards and follow-ups.

jamal: taking over. My immediate todo: keep prefill at 4, monitor fragmentation and evictions, hold traffic shift until p99 stable < 500ms for 15m, coordinate with storage team on defrag window.

sre-lead: assign postmortem owner: elin. Timeline: incident opened 1818001234 (root). Resolved-by 1818004512 (partial recovery). Postmortem draft due in 72h.

elin: accepting ownership of postmortem. I'll gather traces, config diffs (PR #4528), and propose the change list.

maria: support ticket: #INC-9873 created, summary added with affected customers list and suggested CS note.

storage-bot: defrag job scheduled tentative for 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC (low-traffic window). Job-id=defrag-991

jamal: leaving a checklist for my shift:
- monitor p95/p99 for streaming routes (Grafana links)
- watch kv_cache.evictions_per_min and fragmentation
- hold prefill flag at 4 until we've validated
- coordinate with storage for defrag
- escalate if p99 > 700ms or evictions > 1500/min

maria: confirmed, adding my notes to the incident channel and closing the page. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged closed by maria at 2026-03-14T21:48:32Z. Severity: Sev2. Link to runbook and incident doc: <https://redwood-internal/incidents/1818001234>

jamal: thanks, will continue monitoring through my shift. If anything spikes I'll re-open thread.

elin: postmortem plan: root cause = prefill concurrency change causing KV eviction churn + fragmentation exposing tail stalls; corrective action = guardrails on prefill, defrag, improved allocation, and add prefill admission control. Draft will include timeline and customer impact numbers.

maria: thanks team. Good collaboration. :heart:
